title: A Bi-Directional Dual-Path Boost-48V-Buck Hybrid Converter for High-Voltage Power-Transmission Cable in Light-Weight Humanoid Robots
problem: Humanoid robots with distributed actuators consume most energy in limbs while battery is centralized in torso, requiring high-current transmission through thick heavy cables causing large I²R losses.
motivation: Reducing weight in humanoid robots demands high-voltage power transmission to minimize parasitic cable resistance and I²R losses, enabling deployment of high-power limbs without heavy wiring.
method: The robot's centralized battery must power actuators spread throughout its limbs via long cables, which waste energy as resistive heat (heat proportional to current squared). The converter reduces this waste using two stages: a boost stage raises the 48V battery voltage higher, which reduces transmission current and therefore heat loss; a buck stage then lowers voltage back to what the motors need. Both stages are optimized to work efficiently with power flowing in both directions.
key_novelty: Using high-voltage transmission with separate direction-optimized converter stages—stepping voltage up to reduce current losses, then down to motor levels—efficiently powers distributed robot limbs from a centralized battery.
contributions: High-voltage transmission path reducing I²R losses in robot power cables
Dual-path architecture optimizing boost and buck efficiency independently
primary_theme: high-voltage power transmission for distributed robotic actuators
